# HP Prime PPL reference

> One entry per PPL name, and the facts about the HP Prime that no single command owns. Every claim says how it is known. The reference calculator is an HP Prime G2 on firmware 2.4.15515.

Every claim carries one of four labels, strongest first: `G2`, measured on a physical HP Prime G2; `emulator`, run on HP's Virtual Calculator, with the answer kept in [commands/results.tsv](commands/results.tsv); `HP help`, stated in the calculator's built-in help; `unverified`, none of those. How an entry and a fact are written: [format.md](format.md). Ways apps are built, as options and not rules: [patterns.md](patterns.md).

Whether a name exists is looked up in [commands/names.tsv](commands/names.tsv): every name in HP's help, command tree and release notes, with its kind and group, the CAS names included, which get no entry. 706 of the 706 names that get an entry have one so far, so a name listed there and missing here is on HP's list but not yet written up.

Cite a fact by its identifier, such as `ppl.local-limit`, and a command by its name, such as `LEFT`.

Generated by `hpprime docs` from the topic pages and the entries: 143 facts and 706 entries. Edit those, not this file.

## PPL: facts about the language

- [topics/ppl.md](topics/ppl.md): Facts about the language as a whole rather than about one command.
- [ppl.local-limit](topics/ppl.md#ppl.local-limit): One LOCAL statement holds at most 8 variables
- [ppl.local-block-scope](topics/ppl.md#ppl.local-block-scope): A LOCAL lasts until the end of its block
- [ppl.index-call](topics/ppl.md#ppl.index-call): The result of a call cannot be indexed where it is produced
- [ppl.export-initialised](topics/ppl.md#ppl.export-initialised): One EXPORT statement holds at most 8 variables
- [ppl.export-home-variable](topics/ppl.md#ppl.export-home-variable): A variable of Home's cannot be exported, though a function can be called like one
- [ppl.no-end-keywords](topics/ppl.md#ppl.no-end-keywords): END closes everything: there is no ENDIF or ENDFOR
- [ppl.minus-sign](topics/ppl.md#ppl.minus-sign): The calculator writes a negative with the mathematical minus sign
- [ppl.one-based](topics/ppl.md#ppl.one-based): Lists, strings and matrices are indexed from 1
- [ppl.string-index-code](topics/ppl.md#ppl.string-index-code): A string indexed answers a character code, not a character
- [ppl.names-ignore-case](topics/ppl.md#ppl.names-ignore-case): The calculator reads a command's name without regard to case
- [ppl.equality-operators](topics/ppl.md#ppl.equality-operators): == compares, := assigns, <> is not-equal
- [ppl.short-circuit](topics/ppl.md#ppl.short-circuit): AND and OR stop at the side that decides, and IFTE evaluates only the clause that wins
- [ppl.end-semicolon](topics/ppl.md#ppl.end-semicolon): END carries a semicolon
- [ppl.global-index-other-program](topics/ppl.md#ppl.global-index-other-program): Indexing a global from another program is not a compile error
- [ppl.return-in-loop](topics/ppl.md#ppl.return-in-loop): RETURN inside a loop is allowed
- [ppl.letter-digit-names](topics/ppl.md#ppl.letter-digit-names): A letter followed by a digit is a usable name
- [ppl.local-m-matrices](topics/ppl.md#ppl.local-m-matrices): A local called m does not clash with the M0..M9 matrices
- [ppl.locals-initialised-one-line](topics/ppl.md#ppl.locals-initialised-one-line): Locals can be initialised on one line
- [ppl.locals-at-top](topics/ppl.md#ppl.locals-at-top): A LOCAL does not have to be at the top of the BEGIN
- [ppl.i-e-as-locals](topics/ppl.md#ppl.i-e-as-locals): i and e work as local names
- [ppl.imaginary-unit](topics/ppl.md#ppl.imaginary-unit): The imaginary unit goes in as `i` and comes back as a private-use glyph
- [ppl.exponent-glyph](topics/ppl.md#ppl.exponent-glyph): Scientific notation comes back with a glyph of the calculator's own
- [ppl.exact-answers](topics/ppl.md#ppl.exact-answers): Some commands answer exactly, and an exact answer is not a number
- [ppl.type-codes](topics/ppl.md#ppl.type-codes): What TYPE answers
- [ppl.function-always-answers](topics/ppl.md#ppl.function-always-answers): A function always answers something
- [ppl.home-no-parentheses](topics/ppl.md#ppl.home-no-parentheses): On Home, type a function with no arguments without parentheses
- [ppl.call-no-parentheses](topics/ppl.md#ppl.call-no-parentheses): In source, a call with no arguments can leave out its parentheses
- [ppl.getkey-no-parentheses](topics/ppl.md#ppl.getkey-no-parentheses): GETKEY works with and without parentheses in PPL
- [ppl.matrices-by-value](topics/ppl.md#ppl.matrices-by-value): Matrices are passed by value, and only a write costs more with size
- [ppl.expr-empty](topics/ppl.md#ppl.expr-empty): EXPR of an empty string fails
- [ppl.expr-dynamic-access](topics/ppl.md#ppl.expr-dynamic-access): EXPR is how a name is resolved at run time, and it is not free
- [ppl.global-namespace](topics/ppl.md#ppl.global-namespace): Exported names share one namespace with Home
- [ppl.decimal-point](topics/ppl.md#ppl.decimal-point): The decimal point in source is always a dot
- [ppl.compilation-order](topics/ppl.md#ppl.compilation-order): A program only sees another's functions if it was compiled afterwards
- [ppl.check-last-error](topics/ppl.md#ppl.check-last-error): Which bad line Check names depends on what is wrong with it
- [ppl.speed-anchor](topics/ppl.md#ppl.speed-anchor): The one speed figure there is
- [ppl.mu-zero-spelling](topics/ppl.md#ppl.mu-zero-spelling): One name on the list cannot be typed as the list spells it

## Screen, keyboard and touch

- [topics/interface.md](topics/interface.md): Facts about the machine a program draws on and reads from, rather than about one command.
- [interface.geometry](topics/interface.md#interface.geometry): The screen is 320x240, and the soft-key row is the bottom 27 pixels
- [interface.draw-units](topics/interface.md#interface.draw-units): A drawing unit is ten pixels, and the origin is the middle of the screen
- [interface.offscreen-grob](topics/interface.md#interface.offscreen-grob): Drawing straight onto the screen shows the work
- [interface.two-themes](topics/interface.md#interface.two-themes): There are two themes, and in the dark one RECT() leaves black text unreadable
- [interface.textout-width](topics/interface.md#interface.textout-width): TEXTOUT_P overflows unless you pass the width
- [interface.text-measure](topics/interface.md#interface.text-measure): TEXTOUT_P returns the x where it finished, which is how text is measured
- [interface.font-glyphs](topics/interface.md#interface.font-glyphs): Some arrow characters come out of TEXTOUT_P as an empty box
- [interface.input-fields](topics/interface.md#interface.input-fields): What INPUT's field descriptions mean
- [interface.input-modal](topics/interface.md#interface.input-modal): INPUT is modal and builds its labels once
- [interface.getkey-position](topics/interface.md#interface.getkey-position): GETKEY returns a position, not a character
- [interface.key-codes](topics/interface.md#interface.key-codes): The 51 key codes, 0 to 50
- [interface.soft-labels-not-keys](topics/interface.md#interface.soft-labels-not-keys): The six labels along the bottom are not keys
- [interface.draw-then-return](topics/interface.md#interface.draw-then-return): A program that draws and returns loses its screen
- [interface.drain-then-wait](topics/interface.md#interface.drain-then-wait): Waiting for a key means draining the buffer first
- [interface.wait-minus-one](topics/interface.md#interface.wait-minus-one): WAIT(-1) waits for a key, though one program on a G2 saw it not wait
- [interface.wait-events](topics/interface.md#interface.wait-events): WAIT(-1) answers a touch as one list per event, and only the click is a tap
- [interface.mouse-lists](topics/interface.md#interface.mouse-lists): MOUSE returns lists inside lists
- [interface.touch-readings](topics/interface.md#interface.touch-readings): A touch reading is not an event
- [interface.dialog-touch-twice](topics/interface.md#interface.dialog-touch-twice): The touch that closes a dialog arrives again underneath
- [interface.screen-capacity](topics/interface.md#interface.screen-capacity): 20 rows of 40 ordinary characters fit in the small font, with no room to spare

- [libraries.usb-keyboard](topics/libraries.md#libraries.usb-keyboard): A USB keyboard can be read from Python, and nobody here has tried it

## Apps

- [topics/apps.md](topics/apps.md): Facts about the `.hpappdir`, its wrappers and its hooks, rather than about one command.
- [apps.hpappdir-contents](topics/apps.md#apps.hpappdir-contents): What is inside a .hpappdir, and what the sizes say
- [apps.startup-view-byte](topics/apps.md#apps.startup-view-byte): One byte decides whether a Python app opens in your screen or the console
- [apps.icon](topics/apps.md#apps.icon): The icon is 73x74, and the calculator keeps a half-size copy
- [apps.two-kinds](topics/apps.md#apps.two-kinds): A PPL app and a Python app differ in where the code lives
- [apps.hooks](topics/apps.md#apps.hooks): The hooks an app's program can export
- [apps.blank-app-hooks](topics/apps.md#apps.blank-app-hooks): In a blank app the hooks are no use
- [apps.blank-app-keys](topics/apps.md#apps.blank-app-keys): The view keys still arrive as keys
- [apps.exports-tied](topics/apps.md#apps.exports-tied): What an app's program exports is tied to that app
- [apps.wrappers-are-portable](topics/apps.md#apps.wrappers-are-portable): The wrappers carry no name, so four templates cover every app
- [apps.main-py](topics/apps.md#apps.main-py): A Python app runs its file by importing it, and a lone file need not be main.py
- [apps.install](topics/apps.md#apps.install): An app is installed by dragging the folder, never by copying into the mirror
- [apps.generated-and-verified](topics/apps.md#apps.generated-and-verified): What has been verified about an app built from the PC
- [apps.hpapp-not-generated](topics/apps.md#apps.hpapp-not-generated): A .hpapp is copied, not generated
- [apps.empty-hpappprgm-not-a-template](topics/apps.md#apps.empty-hpappprgm-not-a-template): The empty .hpappprgm cannot act as a template
- [apps.function-needs-active-app](topics/apps.md#apps.function-needs-active-app): An app's functions answer only while its app is active
- [apps.qualified-names](topics/apps.md#apps.qualified-names): An app's name in front reaches its variables and functions from another app
- [apps.triangle-solver-degrees](topics/apps.md#apps.triangle-solver-degrees): The Triangle Solver answers in degrees while it is active
- [apps.reset-leaves-function-active](topics/apps.md#apps.reset-leaves-function-active): A reset calculator has the Function app active
- [apps.app-mode-overrides-home](topics/apps.md#apps.app-mode-overrides-home): The active app's mode overrides Home's
- [apps.finance-shows-two-decimals](topics/apps.md#apps.finance-shows-two-decimals): The Finance app turns numbers into text with two decimals

- [topics/micropython.md](topics/micropython.md): Facts about MicroPython on the calculator and the bridge to PPL, rather than about one command.
- [micropython.modules](topics/micropython.md#micropython.modules): What is there and what is not
- [micropython.community-modules](topics/micropython.md#micropython.community-modules): The modules the community documents and nobody here has run

- [micropython.hpprime-undocumented](topics/micropython.md#micropython.hpprime-undocumented): The rest of the hpprime module is not exercised here
- [micropython.eval](topics/micropython.md#micropython.eval): eval() runs PPL and returns numbers and lists of numbers
- [micropython.eval-parentheses](topics/micropython.md#micropython.eval-parentheses): On the Python side, TICKS and GETKEY answer with or without parentheses
- [micropython.list-with-string-closes-the-app](topics/micropython.md#micropython.list-with-string-closes-the-app): A list with a string inside closes the app
- [micropython.string-quotes](topics/micropython.md#micropython.string-quotes): A quote inside a built string breaks the PPL expression
- [micropython.number-notation](topics/micropython.md#micropython.number-notation): Pass numbers through repr(float(x)), not scientific notation
- [micropython.bridge-cost](topics/micropython.md#micropython.bridge-cost): A bridge crossing was timed at 0.2 ms
- [micropython.imports](topics/micropython.md#micropython.imports): A shared module can only import what MicroPython has
- [micropython.mark-debugging](topics/micropython.md#micropython.mark-debugging): When the app closes by itself, leave marks in a PPL global
- [micropython.ppl-calls-python](topics/micropython.md#micropython.ppl-calls-python): PPL can call Python, and it has not been measured here
- [micropython.not-measured](topics/micropython.md#micropython.not-measured): What is still not measured about Python on the Prime

## The file formats

- [topics/formats.md](topics/formats.md): Facts about the files the calculator reads and writes, rather than about one command.
- [formats.container](topics/formats.md#formats.container): The .hpprgm is a nested TLV container
- [formats.source-record](topics/formats.md#formats.source-record): The source record is found by its shape, innermost first
- [formats.wrapper-trap](topics/formats.md#formats.wrapper-trap): A record that wraps the source can read as text too
- [formats.trailer-varies](topics/formats.md#formats.trailer-varies): The trailer is not constant, so it is copied rather than built
- [formats.header-words](topics/formats.md#formats.header-words): Two header words vary between files, and nobody knows what they mean
- [formats.line-endings](topics/formats.md#formats.line-endings): The stored source has LF endings and no trailing newline
- [formats.source-offset-152](topics/formats.md#formats.source-offset-152): Source at offset 152 means no compiled block, which is what a template needs
- [formats.two-producers](topics/formats.md#formats.two-producers): The calculator adds a compiled block to anything it saves
- [formats.block-is-a-cache](topics/formats.md#formats.block-is-a-cache): The compiled block is a cache the calculator rebuilds
- [formats.block-not-byte-stable](topics/formats.md#formats.block-not-byte-stable): The same source compiled twice gives different blocks
- [formats.number](topics/formats.md#formats.number): A number is 8 bytes of BCD with a 12-bit exponent
- [formats.number-infinity](topics/formats.md#formats.number-infinity): Infinity is marked by a sign nibble of its own
- [formats.hpmat](topics/formats.md#formats.hpmat): An .hpmat is that number format with a 16-byte header
- [formats.hpmat-vector](topics/formats.md#formats.hpmat-vector): A vector is the same file with rank 1 and one row
- [formats.symbol-table](topics/formats.md#formats.symbol-table): The compiled block is the program's symbol table, and Main is an entry in it
- [formats.matrix-type-byte](topics/formats.md#formats.matrix-type-byte): A matrix value's type is one byte, and its neighbour is uninitialised
- [formats.value-types-undecoded](topics/formats.md#formats.value-types-undecoded): The value types other than a matrix are not decoded
- [formats.matrix-flag](topics/formats.md#formats.matrix-flag): The flag before a matrix value's type is not the rank
- [formats.entry-splice](topics/formats.md#formats.entry-splice): Where a new symbol entry would be spliced in is not established
- [formats.other-files](topics/formats.md#formats.other-files): What else is in the folder, and what the tools refuse to read

## Getting it onto the calculator

- [topics/deploy.md](topics/deploy.md): Facts about the two destinations -- the emulator and a physical calculator -- rather than about one command.
- [deploy.emulator-folder](topics/deploy.md#deploy.emulator-folder): The emulator's folder really is a mailbox
- [deploy.compile-once-after-a-file-copy](topics/deploy.md#deploy.compile-once-after-a-file-copy): A program that arrives as a file has to be compiled once
- [deploy.results-come-back-on-exit](topics/deploy.md#deploy.results-come-back-on-exit): A matrix written by a program appears when the emulator closes
- [deploy.which-window-opens](topics/deploy.md#deploy.which-window-opens): Which calculator a window opens is decided by lock files
- [deploy.calc-hpsettings-moves](topics/deploy.md#deploy.calc-hpsettings-moves): calc.hpsettings moving says which calculator, not that the window closed
- [deploy.ck-mirror](topics/deploy.md#deploy.ck-mirror): The Connectivity Kit's folder is a mirror, not a drop box
- [deploy.content-library-send](topics/deploy.md#deploy.content-library-send): A physical calculator can receive a file without a drag
- [deploy.ck-offers-firmware](topics/deploy.md#deploy.ck-offers-firmware): The Connectivity Kit can open a firmware update with its update button focused
- [deploy.usb-without-the-ck](topics/deploy.md#deploy.usb-without-the-ck): A program can be pushed over USB without the Connectivity Kit
- [deploy.drag-refused-when-elevated](topics/deploy.md#deploy.drag-refused-when-elevated): A drag refused with the no-entry cursor is Windows, not the file
- [deploy.no-manual-compile](topics/deploy.md#deploy.no-manual-compile): A program dragged over runs without compiling it by hand
- [deploy.read-it-back](topics/deploy.md#deploy.read-it-back): Do not trust that you installed it: read it back
- [deploy.writer-on-hardware](topics/deploy.md#deploy.writer-on-hardware): A program generated on the PC runs on a G2
- [deploy.template-from-the-ck](topics/deploy.md#deploy.template-from-the-ck): A template is a program the Connectivity Kit wrote, and the mirror has almost none
- [deploy.which-calculator-is-which](topics/deploy.md#deploy.which-calculator-is-which): Which calculator a mirror folder belongs to is in its settings file

## A calculator on its USB cable

- [topics/usb.md](topics/usb.md): Facts about reaching a physical HP Prime G2 from a PC over its cable, with no other software in the way: what it is showing, its keys and its programs.
- [usb.device](topics/usb.md#usb.device): A G2 is a HID device, with reports of 1024 bytes
- [usb.one-program-at-a-time](topics/usb.md#usb.one-program-at-a-time): While the Connectivity Kit runs, nothing else can open the calculator
- [usb.frames](topics/usb.md#usb.frames): A message is a sequence number and a command, and a reply adds a size
- [usb.screen](topics/usb.md#usb.screen): The screen comes back as a PNG whose greys are colours
- [usb.keys](topics/usb.md#usb.keys): A key is two reports, and it acts when the second arrives
- [usb.letters](topics/usb.md#usb.letters): A letter is Alpha, or Shift and Alpha, and then the key that carries it
- [usb.start-by-name](topics/usb.md#usb.start-by-name): A name typed over USB and then Enter starts what it names
- [usb.program-message](topics/usb.md#usb.program-message): A program travels as its source, compressed, without its container
- [usb.send-program](topics/usb.md#usb.send-program): A program sent over USB is installed and compiled, with no sign on the screen
- [usb.compile-check](topics/usb.md#usb.compile-check): Whether a program compiled shows when its name is typed on Home
- [usb.file-request](topics/usb.md#usb.file-request): Asking for a file was answered once, and why not since is not known
- [usb.status-area](topics/usb.md#usb.status-area): Keys over USB stop the clock and the battery being drawn
- [usb.newer-framing](topics/usb.md#usb.newer-framing): The newer framing is not what makes a key act
- [usb.kit-window](topics/usb.md#usb.kit-window): The Connectivity Kit shows the screen in a window, and takes no input there

## Commands: advanced-graphing

- [commands/advanced-graphing.md](commands/advanced-graphing.md): all 6 entries of the group on one page
- [NumXStart](commands/advanced-graphing/NumXStart.md): A setting of the Advanced Graphing app's numeric view, 0 on a reset calculator, which a program can set.
- [NumXStep](commands/advanced-graphing/NumXStep.md): A setting of the Advanced Graphing app's numeric view, 0.1 on a reset calculator, which a program can set.
- [NumXZoom](commands/advanced-graphing/NumXZoom.md): A setting of the Advanced Graphing app's numeric view, 2 on a reset calculator, which a program can set.
- [NumYStart](commands/advanced-graphing/NumYStart.md): A setting of the Advanced Graphing app's numeric view, 0 on a reset calculator, which a program can set.
- [NumYStep](commands/advanced-graphing/NumYStep.md): A setting of the Advanced Graphing app's numeric view, 0.1 on a reset calculator, which a program can set.
- [NumYZoom](commands/advanced-graphing/NumYZoom.md): A setting of the Advanced Graphing app's numeric view, 2 on a reset calculator, which a program can set.

## Commands: app

- [commands/app.md](commands/app.md): all 3 entries of the group on one page
- [STARTAPP](commands/app/STARTAPP.md): Starts an app by name.
- [STARTVIEW](commands/app/STARTVIEW.md): Opens one of the current app's views.
- [VIEW](commands/app/VIEW.md): Declares one of an app's own views, with the name it shows in the View menu.

## Commands: arithmetic

- [commands/arithmetic.md](commands/arithmetic.md): all 13 entries of the group on one page
- [%](commands/arithmetic/%.md): A percentage of a value.
- [ALOG](commands/arithmetic/ALOG.md): Ten raised to the value: the antilogarithm.
- [ARG](commands/arithmetic/ARG.md): The angle of a complex number.
- [CONJ](commands/arithmetic/CONJ.md): The complex conjugate: the same number with the imaginary part negated.
- [EXPM1](commands/arithmetic/EXPM1.md): e raised to the value, minus one.
- [FNROOT](commands/arithmetic/FNROOT.md): Finds a value of the variable that makes the expression zero.
- [IM](commands/arithmetic/IM.md): The imaginary part of a complex number.
- [LNP1](commands/arithmetic/LNP1.md): The natural logarithm of one plus the value.
- [MAX](commands/arithmetic/MAX.md): The largest of the values given, or the larger of each pair of two lists.
- [MIN](commands/arithmetic/MIN.md): The smallest of the values given, or the smaller of each pair of two lists.
- [MOD](commands/arithmetic/MOD.md): The remainder after dividing.
- [RE](commands/arithmetic/RE.md): The real part of a complex number.
- [SIGN](commands/arithmetic/SIGN.md): Whether a value is positive, negative or zero.

## Commands: block

- [commands/block.md](commands/block.md): all 3 entries of the group on one page
- [BEGIN](commands/block/BEGIN.md): Opens a function's body, and `END;` closes it.
- [KILL](commands/block/KILL.md): Stops the program that is running.
- [RETURN](commands/block/RETURN.md): Leaves the function, with a value.

## Commands: branch

- [commands/branch.md](commands/branch.md): all 3 entries of the group on one page
- [CASE](commands/branch/CASE.md): Tries each test in turn and runs the first block whose test is true.
- [IF](commands/branch/IF.md): Runs a block when a test is true, and another block when it is not.
- [IFERR](commands/branch/IFERR.md): Runs a block, and runs a second one instead if the first raises an error.

## Commands: catalog

- [commands/catalog.md](commands/catalog.md): all 48 entries of the group on one page
- [ACOS](commands/catalog/ACOS.md): The inverse cosine.
- [ALPHA](commands/catalog/ALPHA.md): On HP's list of names, and refused as a call.
- [ASIN](commands/catalog/ASIN.md): The inverse sine.
- [ATAN](commands/catalog/ATAN.md): The inverse tangent.
- [COLOR](commands/catalog/COLOR.md): Answers its own name back, unevaluated.
- [COS](commands/catalog/COS.md): The cosine.
- [CopyVar](commands/catalog/CopyVar.md): Copies one variable into another.
- [DEBUG](commands/catalog/DEBUG.md): Starts a program under the debugger.
- [Dirac](commands/catalog/Dirac.md): The Dirac delta, which is infinite at zero.
- [DrawSlp](commands/catalog/DrawSlp.md): Answers the line through a point with a given slope.
- [EEX](commands/catalog/EEX.md): On HP's list of names, and refused as a call.
- [EVALLIST](commands/catalog/EVALLIST.md): Evaluates every element of a list.
- [EXP](commands/catalog/EXP.md): e raised to the value.
- [GETBASE](commands/catalog/GETBASE.md): Answers the base a based integer is written in.
- [GF](commands/catalog/GF.md): Builds a Galois field and describes it back as text.
- [Heaviside](commands/catalog/Heaviside.md): The step that is 0 below zero and 1 above it.
- [ICON](commands/catalog/ICON.md): On HP's list of names, and refused as a call.
- [IFTE](commands/catalog/IFTE.md): Answers one of two values, depending on a test.
- [INVERSE](commands/catalog/INVERSE.md): The inverse, refused everything tried here.
- [LN](commands/catalog/LN.md): The natural logarithm.
- [LOG](commands/catalog/LOG.md): The logarithm, base ten unless another base is given.
- [LineHorz](commands/catalog/LineHorz.md): Answers a horizontal line, as an equation.
- [LineTan](commands/catalog/LineTan.md): The tangent to a curve, which needs its expression kept back.
- [LineVert](commands/catalog/LineVert.md): Answers a vertical line, as an equation.
- [MAXREAL](commands/catalog/MAXREAL.md): The largest real the calculator holds.
- [MEMORY](commands/catalog/MEMORY.md): Answers two figures about the calculator's memory.
- [MINREAL](commands/catalog/MINREAL.md): The smallest positive real the calculator holds.
- [NEG](commands/catalog/NEG.md): Negation, refused when it is written as a call.
- [NTHROOT](commands/catalog/NTHROOT.md): The nth root, written between the degree and the number.
- [PI](commands/catalog/PI.md): The constant pi.
- [PIECEWISE](commands/catalog/PIECEWISE.md): Answers the case whose test is true.
- [POLYCOEF](commands/catalog/POLYCOEF.md): The coefficients of the polynomial with the given roots.
- [POLYEVAL](commands/catalog/POLYEVAL.md): Works a polynomial out at a value.
- [POLYROOT](commands/catalog/POLYROOT.md): The roots of a polynomial.
- [QPI](commands/catalog/QPI.md): Turns a decimal into an exact form, as a fraction or a multiple of pi.
- [QUOTE](commands/catalog/QUOTE.md): Hands back an expression without evaluating it.
- [SERIAL](commands/catalog/SERIAL.md): Answers this calculator's serial number, which is never stored here.
- [SIN](commands/catalog/SIN.md): The sine.
- [SUPPRESS](commands/catalog/SUPPRESS.md): Removes the element at a position.
- [TAN](commands/catalog/TAN.md): The tangent.
- [UTPC](commands/catalog/UTPC.md): The upper tail of a chi-square distribution, refused as written here.
- [UTPF](commands/catalog/UTPF.md): The upper tail of a Fisher distribution, refused as written here.
- [UTPN](commands/catalog/UTPN.md): The upper tail of a normal distribution, refused as written here.
- [UTPT](commands/catalog/UTPT.md): The upper tail of a Student distribution, refused as written here.
- [VERSION](commands/catalog/VERSION.md): Answers the software version, and the serial number with it.
- [ΔLIST](commands/catalog/ΔLIST.md): The differences between neighbouring elements of a list.
- [Σ](commands/catalog/Σ.md): The sum of an expression over a range.
- [ΣLIST](commands/catalog/ΣLIST.md): The sum of every element of a list.

## Commands: common-app-mode

- [commands/common-app-mode.md](commands/common-app-mode.md): all 4 entries of the group on one page
- [AAngle](commands/common-app-mode/AAngle.md): The active app's angle mode: 0 leaves it to Home, 1 is radians and 2 degrees, and a program on Home follows it.
- [AComplex](commands/common-app-mode/AComplex.md): The active app's setting for complex numbers: 0 leaves it to Home, and at 2 a program on Home gets complex answers.
- [ADigits](commands/common-app-mode/ADigits.md): The active app's number of digits, 4 on a reset calculator, which STRING follows once the app's format is fixed.
- [AFormat](commands/common-app-mode/AFormat.md): The active app's number format: 0 leaves it to Home, and at 2 STRING writes a fixed number of decimals.

- [is_conjugate](commands/geometry/is_conjugate.md): Whether points are conjugate with respect to a circle.
- [is_element](commands/geometry/is_element.md): Whether a point lies on an object.
- [is_equilateral](commands/geometry/is_equilateral.md): Whether a triangle has three equal sides.
- [is_isosceles](commands/geometry/is_isosceles.md): Answers which pair of sides is equal, not whether any is.
- [is_orthogonal](commands/geometry/is_orthogonal.md): Whether two lines meet at a right angle.
- [is_parallelogram](commands/geometry/is_parallelogram.md): Answers a code for the kind of quadrilateral, not a yes or no.
- [is_perpendicular](commands/geometry/is_perpendicular.md): Whether two lines are perpendicular, which this example cannot tell from is_orthogonal.
- [isopolygon](commands/geometry/isopolygon.md): A regular polygon, whose answer is long enough to be cut.
- [line](commands/geometry/line.md): Refused, where the two commands beside it answered.
- [locus](commands/geometry/locus.md): The path a point traces, refused for the two points given.
- [median_line](commands/geometry/median_line.md): The line from a vertex to the middle of the opposite side.
- [midpoint](commands/geometry/midpoint.md): The middle of a segment.
- [ordinate](commands/geometry/ordinate.md): The y coordinate of a point.
- [parabola](commands/geometry/parabola.md): A parabola, answered as a parametric plot.
- [parallel](commands/geometry/parallel.md): The parallel to a line through a point.
- [parallelogram](commands/geometry/parallelogram.md): A parallelogram from three of its vertices.
- [parameq](commands/geometry/parameq.md): The parametric equation of an object, refused for the line tried here.
- [perimeter](commands/geometry/perimeter.md): The perimeter of a polygon, refused because its argument was.
- [perpen_bisector](commands/geometry/perpen_bisector.md): The perpendicular through the middle of a segment.
- [perpendicular](commands/geometry/perpendicular.md): The perpendicular through a point, which asked for three points instead.
- [plotfield](commands/geometry/plotfield.md): Refused, quoting the call back in its answer.
- [plotfunc](commands/geometry/plotfunc.md): Rewrites a function as a parametric plot.
- [plotimplicit](commands/geometry/plotimplicit.md): Answered an empty list.
- [plotlist](commands/geometry/plotlist.md): Joins a matrix of points into a segment.
- [plotode](commands/geometry/plotode.md): Refused, quoting the call back in its answer.
- [plotparam](commands/geometry/plotparam.md): Refused, though two other commands answer by building one.
- [plotpolar](commands/geometry/plotpolar.md): Rewrites a polar expression as a parametric plot.
- [plotseq](commands/geometry/plotseq.md): Answers the whole staircase of a sequence, and overflowed the row.
- [point](commands/geometry/point.md): Builds a point from two coordinates.
- [polar_coordinates](commands/geometry/polar_coordinates.md): A point's radius and angle, as a vector.
- [polygon](commands/geometry/polygon.md): A closed figure through any number of points.
- [projection](commands/geometry/projection.md): The foot of the perpendicular from a point to a curve.
- [quadrilateral](commands/geometry/quadrilateral.md): A four-sided figure through four points.
- [radius](commands/geometry/radius.md): The radius of a circle.
- [randNorm](commands/geometry/randNorm.md): A random point, which cannot have an example.
- [reciprocation](commands/geometry/reciprocation.md): The polar line of a point with respect to a circle.
- [rectangle](commands/geometry/rectangle.md): A rectangle on a side, with the second side given as a ratio.
- [reflection](commands/geometry/reflection.md): Reflects an object in a line.
- [rhombus](commands/geometry/rhombus.md): A rhombus on a side, with the angle given in radians.
- [right_triangle](commands/geometry/right_triangle.md): A right triangle on a leg, with the other leg given as a ratio.
- [rotation](commands/geometry/rotation.md): Turns an object about a centre, answering a complex exponential.
- [segment](commands/geometry/segment.md): The segment between two points.
- [similarity](commands/geometry/similarity.md): Scales and turns an object about a centre.
- [single_inter](commands/geometry/single_inter.md): One intersection of two curves, which came back as an error message.
- [slope](commands/geometry/slope.md): The slope of a line, or of the line through two points.
- [square](commands/geometry/square.md): The square on a side given by two points.
- [tangent](commands/geometry/tangent.md): The tangent to a curve, which answered an empty list.
- [translation](commands/geometry/translation.md): Moves an object by a vector, and says so when given a point instead.
- [triangle](commands/geometry/triangle.md): Refused, where every other polygon constructor answered.
- [zoomauto](commands/geometry/zoomauto.md): Refused, with the whole zoom family.
- [zoombox](commands/geometry/zoombox.md): Refused, with the whole zoom family.
- [zoomdecimal](commands/geometry/zoomdecimal.md): Refused, with the whole zoom family.
- [zoomdundo](commands/geometry/zoomdundo.md): Refused, with the whole zoom family.
- [zoomin](commands/geometry/zoomin.md): Refused, with the whole zoom family.
- [zoominteger](commands/geometry/zoominteger.md): Refused, with the whole zoom family.
- [zoomout](commands/geometry/zoomout.md): Refused, with the whole zoom family.

## Commands: home-settings

- [commands/home-settings.md](commands/home-settings.md): all 9 entries of the group on one page
- [Base](commands/home-settings/Base.md): The base Home writes integers in: 3, hexadecimal, on a reset calculator.
- [Bits](commands/home-settings/Bits.md): The size in bits of Home's integers, 32 on a reset calculator.
- [Entry](commands/home-settings/Entry.md): Home's entry mode, 0 on a reset calculator.
- [HAngle](commands/home-settings/HAngle.md): The angle mode of Home: 0 is radians and 1 is degrees.
- [HComplex](commands/home-settings/HComplex.md): Whether Home answers with complex numbers: at 0 the square root of a negative is refused, at 1 it is imaginary.
- [HDigits](commands/home-settings/HDigits.md): How many decimal places Home's fixed format shows, 8 on a reset calculator.
- [HFormat](commands/home-settings/HFormat.md): How Home writes numbers: 0, the standard format, on a reset calculator, and 1 for a fixed number of decimals.
- [HSeparator](commands/home-settings/HSeparator.md): A Home setting for how numbers are separated, 0 on a reset calculator.
- [Signed](commands/home-settings/Signed.md): Whether Home's integers are signed, 0 on a reset calculator.

## Commands: inference

- [commands/inference.md](commands/inference.md): all 59 entries of the group on one page
- [Alpha](commands/inference/Alpha.md): The significance level: refused bare with the wrong app, set and kept with its own.
- [AltHyp](commands/inference/AltHyp.md): Which alternative hypothesis the test uses.
- [AnovaOneWay](commands/inference/AnovaOneWay.md): One-way analysis of variance over any number of samples.
- [Chi2GOF](commands/inference/Chi2GOF.md): The chi-square goodness-of-fit test, refused for the arguments given.
- [Chi2TwoWay](commands/inference/Chi2TwoWay.md): The chi-square test on a table of counts.
- [Conf](commands/inference/Conf.md): The confidence level, which arrived at 0.99.
- [ContribList](commands/inference/ContribList.md): Empty, and holds each cell’s contribution to the chi-square statistic.
- [ContribMat](commands/inference/ContribMat.md): A one-by-one zero matrix, and holds each cell’s contribution in a two-way table.
- [CritScore](commands/inference/CritScore.md): The critical value of the test statistic.
- [CritVal1](commands/inference/CritVal1.md): The first critical value, 0 until DoInference put 0.432843347747 in it.
- [CritVal2](commands/inference/CritVal2.md): The second critical value, unread after the run.
- [DF](commands/inference/DF.md): The degrees of freedom.
- [DFerr](commands/inference/DFerr.md): The error degrees of freedom of an analysis of variance.
- [DataType](commands/inference/DataType.md): Which shape of data the app is set to read.
- [DoInference](commands/inference/DoInference.md): Runs the Inference app's own test and writes the results into the app's variables.
- [ExpList](commands/inference/ExpList.md): Empty, and holds the expected counts a goodness-of-fit test compares against.
- [ExpMat](commands/inference/ExpMat.md): A one-by-one zero matrix, and holds the expected counts of a two-way table.
- [Fval](commands/inference/Fval.md): The F statistic of an analysis of variance.
- [InfType](commands/inference/InfType.md): Which inference the app is set to perform.
- [Inter](commands/inference/Inter.md): The intercept of a fitted line.
- [LinRegrTConfInt](commands/inference/LinRegrTConfInt.md): A confidence interval for a linear regression.
- [LinRegrTConfSlope](commands/inference/LinRegrTConfSlope.md): A confidence interval for the slope of a linear regression.
- [LinRegrTMeanResp](commands/inference/LinRegrTMeanResp.md): An interval for the mean response at a value, indistinguishable here from LinRegrTPredInt.
- [LinRegrTPredInt](commands/inference/LinRegrTPredInt.md): A prediction interval at a value, indistinguishable here from LinRegrTMeanResp.
- [LinRegrTTest](commands/inference/LinRegrTTest.md): The t test on a linear regression, refused for the arguments given.
- [MS](commands/inference/MS.md): The mean square of an analysis of variance.
- [MSerr](commands/inference/MSerr.md): The error mean square of an analysis of variance.
- [Mean₁](commands/inference/Mean₁.md): The first sample mean, 0.461368 before anything was asked.
- [Mean₂](commands/inference/Mean₂.md): The second sample mean, 0.522851 before anything was asked.
- [Method](commands/inference/Method.md): Which method the chosen inference uses.
- [ObsList](commands/inference/ObsList.md): Empty, and holds the observed counts of a goodness-of-fit test.
- [ObsMat](commands/inference/ObsMat.md): A one-by-one zero matrix, and holds the observed counts of a two-way table.
- [Pooled](commands/inference/Pooled.md): Whether the two variances are pooled.
- [Prob](commands/inference/Prob.md): The p-value, 0 until DoInference put 0.172021922639 in it.
- [ProbList](commands/inference/ProbList.md): Empty, and holds the hypothesised probabilities of a goodness-of-fit test.
- [Result](commands/inference/Result.md): A code DoInference wrote 1 into, and nothing says what 1 means.
- [SS](commands/inference/SS.md): The sum of squares of an analysis of variance.
- [SSerr](commands/inference/SSerr.md): The error sum of squares of an analysis of variance.
- [TestScore](commands/inference/TestScore.md): The test statistic, 0 until DoInference put −0.946205374811 in it.
- [TestValue](commands/inference/TestValue.md): The hypothesised value the test is measured against.
- [Xlist](commands/inference/Xlist.md): An Inference list that answers `{}` with another app active, as the app's other five lists do.
- [Xval](commands/inference/Xval.md): A value of x to predict from a fitted line.
- [Ylist](commands/inference/Ylist.md): The second data list, and the one that proved a list can be assigned.
- [Yval](commands/inference/Yval.md): A value of y predicted from a fitted line.
- [coefDet](commands/inference/coefDet.md): The coefficient of determination of a fitted line.
- [corr](commands/inference/corr.md): The correlation of a fitted line.
- [n₁](commands/inference/n₁.md): The first sample size, 50 in the app’s loaded example.
- [n₂](commands/inference/n₂.md): The second sample size, also 50.
- [serrInter](commands/inference/serrInter.md): The standard error of the intercept.
- [serrLine](commands/inference/serrLine.md): The standard error of the fitted line.
- [serrSlope](commands/inference/serrSlope.md): The standard error of the slope.
- [s₁](commands/inference/s₁.md): The first sample standard deviation, 0.2776.
- [s₂](commands/inference/s₂.md): The second sample standard deviation, 0.2943.
- [x₁](commands/inference/x₁.md): The first count, 21 of 50 in the loaded example.
- [x₂](commands/inference/x₂.md): The second count, 26 of 50.
- [μ₀](commands/inference/μ₀.md): Refused as HP spells it, and the calculator wants a different codepoint.
- [π₀](commands/inference/π₀.md): The null-hypothesis proportion, which arrived at 0.5 and spells correctly.
- [σ₁](commands/inference/σ₁.md): The first population deviation, 0.2887.
- [σ₂](commands/inference/σ₂.md): The second population deviation, equal to the first.

- [diag](commands/matrix/diag.md): Takes the diagonal out of a matrix, or builds a matrix from a diagonal.
- [hessenberg](commands/matrix/hessenberg.md): The Hessenberg reduction of a matrix.

- [l2norm](commands/matrix/l2norm.md): The Euclidean length of a vector.

- [pivot](commands/matrix/pivot.md): One step of Gaussian elimination.

## Commands: probability

- [commands/probability.md](commands/probability.md): all 28 entries of the group on one page
- [!](commands/probability/!.md): Factorial: the product of every whole number up to this one.
- [BINOMIAL](commands/probability/BINOMIAL.md): The probability of exactly k successes in n tries.
- [BINOMIAL_CDF](commands/probability/BINOMIAL_CDF.md): The probability of k successes or fewer in n tries.

- [CHISQUARE_ICDF](commands/probability/CHISQUARE_ICDF.md): The point a chi-squared distribution reaches a probability at.
- [COMB](commands/probability/COMB.md): How many ways to choose r things from n, order not counting.
- [FISHER](commands/probability/FISHER.md): The F density at a point.

- [FISHER_ICDF](commands/probability/FISHER_ICDF.md): The point an F distribution reaches a probability at.

- [NORMALD](commands/probability/NORMALD.md): The normal density at a point.
- [NORMALD_CDF](commands/probability/NORMALD_CDF.md): The probability that a normal value is at or below a point.
- [NORMALD_ICDF](commands/probability/NORMALD_ICDF.md): The point a normal distribution reaches a given probability at.
- [PERM](commands/probability/PERM.md): How many ways to arrange r things out of n, order counting.
- [POISSON](commands/probability/POISSON.md): The probability of exactly k events when μ are expected.
- [POISSON_CDF](commands/probability/POISSON_CDF.md): The probability of k events or fewer when μ are expected.
- [POISSON_ICDF](commands/probability/POISSON_ICDF.md): The count a Poisson distribution reaches a probability at.
- [RANDINT](commands/probability/RANDINT.md): A random whole number.
- [RANDNORM](commands/probability/RANDNORM.md): A random number from a normal distribution.
- [RANDOM](commands/probability/RANDOM.md): A random number.
- [RANDSEED](commands/probability/RANDSEED.md): Sets the starting point of the random sequence.
- [STUDENT](commands/probability/STUDENT.md): The Student's t density at a point.
- [STUDENT_CDF](commands/probability/STUDENT_CDF.md): The probability that a Student's t value is at or below a point.
- [STUDENT_ICDF](commands/probability/STUDENT_ICDF.md): The point a Student's t distribution reaches a probability at.
- [geometric_cdf](commands/probability/geometric_cdf.md): The probability that the first success comes on try k or earlier.
- [geometric_icdf](commands/probability/geometric_icdf.md): The try a geometric distribution reaches a probability at.

## Commands: sequence

- [commands/sequence.md](commands/sequence.md): all 1 entry of the group on one page
- [SeqPlot](commands/sequence/SeqPlot.md): A Sequence app setting, 0 on a reset calculator; assigning 1 raised nothing and left it at 0.

- [Solve](commands/solve/Solve.md): Refused in six forms: with and without its own app active, and with its app's name in front.

- [Ei](commands/special/Ei.md): The exponential integral.

- [Psi](commands/special/Psi.md): The polygamma function.

- [Zeta](commands/special/Zeta.md): The Riemann zeta function.
- [erf](commands/special/erf.md): The error function.
- [erfc](commands/special/erfc.md): The complementary error function.

## Commands: spreadsheet

- [commands/spreadsheet.md](commands/spreadsheet.md): all 26 entries of the group on one page
- [AMORT](commands/spreadsheet/AMORT.md): An amortisation table into a range, refused from Home.
- [AVERAGE](commands/spreadsheet/AVERAGE.md): The mean of a list, once the Spreadsheet app is active.
- [CellHasData](commands/spreadsheet/CellHasData.md): Says whether the current cell holds anything, and answers 0 on an empty sheet.
- [ClearCell](commands/spreadsheet/ClearCell.md): Empties the current cell, and answers 0 with the app active.
- [Col](commands/spreadsheet/Col.md): A Spreadsheet variable, 0 on a reset calculator, which a program cannot set.
- [ColWidth](commands/spreadsheet/ColWidth.md): A Spreadsheet setting, −1 on a reset calculator, which a program can set.
- [ConfT1mean](commands/spreadsheet/ConfT1mean.md): A t confidence interval for one mean, refused from Home.
- [ConfT2mean](commands/spreadsheet/ConfT2mean.md): A t confidence interval for two means, refused from Home.
- [ConfZ1mean](commands/spreadsheet/ConfZ1mean.md): A z confidence interval for one mean, refused from Home.
- [ConfZ1prop](commands/spreadsheet/ConfZ1prop.md): A z confidence interval for one proportion, refused from Home.
- [ConfZ2mean](commands/spreadsheet/ConfZ2mean.md): A z confidence interval for two means, refused from Home.
- [ConfZ2prop](commands/spreadsheet/ConfZ2prop.md): A z confidence interval for two proportions, refused from Home.
- [HypT1mean](commands/spreadsheet/HypT1mean.md): A t test for one mean, refused from Home.
- [HypT2mean](commands/spreadsheet/HypT2mean.md): A t test for two means, refused from Home.
- [HypZ1mean](commands/spreadsheet/HypZ1mean.md): A z test for one mean, refused from Home.
- [HypZ1prop](commands/spreadsheet/HypZ1prop.md): A z test for one proportion, refused from Home.
- [HypZ2mean](commands/spreadsheet/HypZ2mean.md): A z test for two means, refused from Home.
- [HypZ2prop](commands/spreadsheet/HypZ2prop.md): A z test for two proportions, refused from Home.
- [PredX](commands/spreadsheet/PredX.md): Predicts an x from a y and a fitted model, refused from Home.
- [PredY](commands/spreadsheet/PredY.md): Predicts a y from an x and a fitted model, refused from Home.
- [REGRS](commands/spreadsheet/REGRS.md): A regression over a range, refused from Home.
- [Row](commands/spreadsheet/Row.md): A Spreadsheet variable, 0 on a reset calculator, which a program cannot set.
- [RowHeight](commands/spreadsheet/RowHeight.md): A Spreadsheet setting, −1 on a reset calculator, which a program can set.
- [STAT1](commands/spreadsheet/STAT1.md): One-variable statistics over a range, refused from Home.
- [STAT2](commands/spreadsheet/STAT2.md): Two-variable statistics over a range, refused from Home.
- [SUM](commands/spreadsheet/SUM.md): Adds up a list; refused unless the Spreadsheet app is active or named in front of it.

## Commands: statistics-1var

- [commands/statistics-1var.md](commands/statistics-1var.md): all 22 entries of the group on one page
- [CHECK](commands/statistics-1var/CHECK.md): Turns on one of the statistics app's analyses.
- [Do1VStats](commands/statistics-1var/Do1VStats.md): Computes the one-variable statistics of an analysis and writes them into the app's variables; answers 1.
- [Hmax](commands/statistics-1var/Hmax.md): A setting of the Statistics 1Var app, 24 on a reset calculator, which a program can set.
- [Hmin](commands/statistics-1var/Hmin.md): A setting of the Statistics 1Var app, 0 on a reset calculator, which a program can set.
- [Hwidth](commands/statistics-1var/Hwidth.md): A setting of the Statistics 1Var app, 1 on a reset calculator, which a program can set.
- [ISCHECK](commands/statistics-1var/ISCHECK.md): Says whether one of the statistics app's analyses is on.
- [MaxVal](commands/statistics-1var/MaxVal.md): The largest data value of the Statistics 1Var data, which Do1VStats writes: 7 for {1,2,2,3,7}.
- [MeanX](commands/statistics-1var/MeanX.md): The mean of the Statistics 1Var data, which Do1VStats writes: 3 for {1,2,2,3,7}.
- [MedVal](commands/statistics-1var/MedVal.md): The median of the Statistics 1Var data, which Do1VStats writes: 2 for {1,2,2,3,7}.
- [MinVal](commands/statistics-1var/MinVal.md): The smallest data value of the Statistics 1Var data, which Do1VStats writes: 1 for {1,2,2,3,7}.
- [NbItem](commands/statistics-1var/NbItem.md): The number of data points of the Statistics 1Var data, which Do1VStats writes: 5 for {1,2,2,3,7}.
- [Q₁](commands/statistics-1var/Q₁.md): The first quartile of the Statistics 1Var data, which Do1VStats writes: 1.5 for {1,2,2,3,7}.
- [Q₃](commands/statistics-1var/Q₃.md): The third quartile of the Statistics 1Var data, which Do1VStats writes: 5 for {1,2,2,3,7}.
- [SetFreq](commands/statistics-1var/SetFreq.md): Points a data set's frequencies at a column, refused on a reset calculator.
- [SetSample](commands/statistics-1var/SetSample.md): Points a data set at a column, refused on a reset calculator.
- [UNCHECK](commands/statistics-1var/UNCHECK.md): Turns off one of the statistics app's analyses.
- [sX](commands/statistics-1var/sX.md): The sample standard deviation of the Statistics 1Var data, which Do1VStats writes: 2.34520787991 for {1,2,2,3,7}.
- [serrX](commands/statistics-1var/serrX.md): The standard error of the mean of the Statistics 1Var data, which Do1VStats writes: 1.04880884817 for {1,2,2,3,7}.
- [ssX](commands/statistics-1var/ssX.md): The sum of the squared deviations from the mean of the Statistics 1Var data, which Do1VStats writes: 22 for {1,2,2,3,7}.
- [ΣX](commands/statistics-1var/ΣX.md): The sum of the data of the Statistics 1Var data, which Do1VStats writes: 15 for {1,2,2,3,7}.
- [ΣX2](commands/statistics-1var/ΣX2.md): The sum of the squares of the data of the Statistics 1Var data, which Do1VStats writes: 67 for {1,2,2,3,7}.
- [σX](commands/statistics-1var/σX-var.md): The population standard deviation of the Statistics 1Var data, which Do1VStats writes: 2.09761769634 for {1,2,2,3,7}.

- [SetIndep](commands/statistics-2var/SetIndep.md): Points a data set's independent column, refused on a reset calculator.
- [residue](commands/statistics-2var/residue.md): The residue of a function, which reports its own failure as text.
- [sCov](commands/statistics-2var/sCov.md): The sample covariance of the Statistics 2Var data, which Do2VStats writes: refused until the app has data.

- [serrY](commands/statistics-2var/serrY.md): The standard error of the mean of the second column of the Statistics 2Var data, which Do2VStats writes: refused until the app has data.

- [ΣXY](commands/statistics-2var/ΣXY.md): The sum of the products of the pairs of the Statistics 2Var data, which Do2VStats writes: refused until the app has data.
- [ΣY](commands/statistics-2var/ΣY.md): The sum of the second column of the Statistics 2Var data, which Do2VStats writes: refused until the app has data.
- [ΣY2](commands/statistics-2var/ΣY2.md): The sum of the squares of the second column of the Statistics 2Var data, which Do2VStats writes: refused until the app has data.
- [σCov](commands/statistics-2var/σCov.md): The population covariance of the Statistics 2Var data, which Do2VStats writes: refused until the app has data.
- [σY](commands/statistics-2var/σY-var.md): The population standard deviation of the second column of the Statistics 2Var data, which Do2VStats writes: refused until the app has data.

## Commands: strings

- [commands/strings.md](commands/strings.md): all 13 entries of the group on one page
- [ASC](commands/strings/ASC.md): The character codes of a string, as a list.
- [CHAR](commands/strings/CHAR.md): The string built from one character code or from a list of them.
- [DIM](commands/strings/DIM.md): How long a string is, or the dimensions of a matrix.
- [EXPR](commands/strings/EXPR.md): Evaluates a string as if it had been typed.
- [INSTRING](commands/strings/INSTRING.md): Where one string first appears inside another.
- [LEFT](commands/strings/LEFT.md): The first n characters of a string.
- [LOWER](commands/strings/LOWER.md): The string in lower case.
- [MID](commands/strings/MID.md): Part of a string: from a start position, a given number of characters or up to the end.
- [RIGHT](commands/strings/RIGHT.md): The last n characters of a string.
- [ROTATE](commands/strings/ROTATE.md): Moves the characters of a string around by n places.
- [STRING](commands/strings/STRING.md): Turns a value into text.
- [STRINGFROMID](commands/strings/STRINGFROMID.md): The calculator's own message for a system message number.
- [UPPER](commands/strings/UPPER.md): The string in upper case.

## Commands: system

- [commands/system.md](commands/system.md): all 9 entries of the group on one page
- [Date](commands/system/Date.md): Today's date as a real, the year before the point and the month and day after it.
- [DelHVars](commands/system/DelHVars.md): On HP's list of names, and the one use of it tried was refused.
- [HVars](commands/system/HVars.md): The names of the variables created on Home, as a list.
- [Language](commands/system/Language.md): The calculator's language, as a number.
- [Notes](commands/system/Notes.md): The names of the notes on the calculator, as a list.
- [Programs](commands/system/Programs.md): The names of the programs on the calculator, as a list of strings.
- [TOff](commands/system/TOff.md): The time before the calculator turns itself off, 300000 on a reset calculator.
- [Theme](commands/system/Theme.md): The display theme, as a list of two integers.
- [Time](commands/system/Time.md): The time of day, a real that STRING writes in hours, minutes and seconds.

- [SAS](commands/triangle-solver/SAS.md): Two sides and the angle between them.
- [SSA](commands/triangle-solver/SSA.md): Two sides and an angle not between them, the ambiguous case.
- [SSS](commands/triangle-solver/SSS.md): Solves a triangle from three sides, in degrees while its app is active.
- [SideA](commands/triangle-solver/SideA.md): The side opposite angle A, and a program can both read it and set it.
- [SideB](commands/triangle-solver/SideB.md): The side opposite angle B.
- [SideC](commands/triangle-solver/SideC.md): The side opposite angle C.
- [TriType](commands/triangle-solver/TriType.md): The one variable of this app that DoSolve left alone.
